_comment: Sits outside `expo`, where Expo ignores it. PORTRAIT (v0.7.3): the top-level `orientation` is the real lock — it writes the supported orientations into the iOS Info.plist and the Android manifest, so a build is never offered a landscape frame. It only applies to a build, which is why utils/orientation.js also locks at runtime for Expo Go. `ios.requireFullScreen` is not optional alongside it: without it iPad keeps Slide Over and Split View, and iOS refuses the orientation lock outright. `userInterfaceStyle` is already Expo's default; it is stated because this app has only a light palette and nothing should be able to put it into dark mode. SUPPORTS TABLET is deliberately false — iPhone only. That is what keeps iPad screenshots off the App Store Connect requirement list and stops a reviewer finding something broken on a screen size this app was never designed for; iPad can be its own release later. BUNDLE IDENTIFIER and `android.package` are permanent once published — Apple will not let the identifier change after the first submission. NEW ARCHITECTURE is on because it is the SDK 54 default; if the first build behaves strangely in a way the Expo Go version did not, this is the first thing to suspect. VERSION is what users see; `buildNumber` and `versionCode` are what the stores count, and eas.json increments them per build. USES NON EXEMPT ENCRYPTION (v0.9.1) writes ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption into the Info.plist, which answers Apple's export-compliance question at upload instead of at a prompt. Without it every build lands in App Store Connect flagged 'Missing Compliance' and cannot be sent to a single tester until someone answers by hand — per build, not once. `false` is the answer for an app whose only encryption is HTTPS through the OS, which is all this one does: Supabase over TLS and nothing else.
